name: 沃尔夫冈·阿马德乌斯·莫扎特

points.title: 神童时期
points.description: 1756年1月27日，莫扎特出生于萨尔茨堡，父亲利奥波德是小提琴家和作曲家。莫扎特自幼展现出非凡的音乐天赋，3岁起就能辨识音符，4岁开始作曲，5岁已能熟练演奏羽管键琴和小提琴。1762年起，父亲带着年幼的莫扎特和姐姐南妮尔在欧洲各地进行巡回演出，先后前往慕尼黑、维也纳、巴黎、伦敦等地，引起轰动。这段经历极大地开阔了莫扎特的视野，但也使他的童年充满了压力和奔波。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Salzburg on January 27, 1756, Mozart showed extraordinary musical talent from an early age. By age 3, he could recognize notes, began composing at 4, and mastered keyboard and violin by 5. From 1762, his father Leopold took him and his sister Nannerl on extensive tours across Europe, including Munich, Vienna, Paris, and London, where they caused sensations. These experiences broadened Mozart's horizons but also subjected his childhood to intense pressure and constant travel.

points.title: 初试歌剧创作
points.description: 1767年，莫扎特随家人首次来到维也纳，并创作了他的第一部歌剧《阿波罗与雅辛托斯》。在此期间，他感染天花但幸运康复。1769年，13岁的莫扎特被任命为萨尔茨堡宫廷乐师，但这一职位限制了他的创作自由。尽管如此，他仍创作了多部歌剧、交响曲和宗教音乐，包括著名的《卢契奥·西拉》和《牧羊王》。这段时间的作品已显示出他独特的音乐风格和对歌剧形式的深刻理解，为后来的创作奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1767, Mozart first visited Vienna with his family and composed his first opera, 'Apollo et Hyacinthus.' During this time, he contracted smallpox but recovered. At 13, he was appointed as a court musician in Salzburg, a position that limited his creative freedom. Nevertheless, he composed numerous operas, symphonies, and religious works, including 'Mitridate, Re di Ponto' and 'Il re pastore.' These works already displayed his unique musical style and deep understanding of opera, laying the foundation for his later compositions.

points.title: 宫廷乐师生涯
points.description: 1773年，莫扎特回到萨尔茨堡，担任大主教宫廷乐师。这一时期，他创作了多部重要作品，包括第25交响曲、第9钢琴协奏曲和《后宫诱逃》等。然而，与大主教的矛盾日益加深，莫扎特对宫廷生活的束缚感到不满，渴望获得更大的创作自由和更高级别的职位。1781年，莫扎特前往维也纳为皇帝约瑟夫二世创作歌剧，与大主教决裂，最终辞去萨尔茨堡的职位，选择成为一名自由作曲家，这一决定改变了他的人生轨迹。
points.descriptionEn: Returning to Salzburg in 1773, Mozart served as court musician to the Archbishop. During this period, he composed significant works including Symphony No. 25, Piano Concerto No. 9, and 'The Abduction from the Seraglio.' However, his conflicts with the Archbishop intensified as Mozart grew dissatisfied with the constraints of court life and yearned for greater creative freedom. In 1781, Mozart traveled to Vienna to compose an opera for Emperor Joseph II, broke with the Archbishop, and eventually resigned from his Salzburg position, choosing to become a freelance composer—a decision that transformed his career path.

points.title: 自由作曲家
points.description: 1781年，莫扎特定居维也纳，开始了作为自由作曲家的生涯。他最初依靠教学、演奏和创作维生，逐渐在维也纳音乐界建立了声誉。这一时期，他创作了多部钢琴协奏曲、弦乐四重奏和歌剧，包括著名的《费加罗的婚礼》(1786)，这部作品在布拉格首演获得巨大成功。1784年，莫扎特加入共济会，这一组织对他的思想和创作产生了深远影响。然而，尽管艺术成就斐然，莫扎特的经济状况并不稳定，常常陷入财务困境。
points.descriptionEn: Settling in Vienna in 1781, Mozart began his career as a freelance composer. Initially supporting himself through teaching, performing, and composing, he gradually established his reputation in Vienna's musical circles. During this period, he composed numerous piano concertos, string quartets, and operas, including the famous 'The Marriage of Figaro' (1786), which premiered to great success in Prague. In 1784, Mozart joined the Freemasonry, an organization that profoundly influenced his thinking and compositions. Despite his artistic achievements, Mozart's financial situation remained unstable, often plagued by financial difficulties.

points.title: 创作巅峰与逝世
points.description: 1787年，莫扎特被任命为皇帝的室内作曲家，获得了一定的经济保障。这一时期是他创作的巅峰，完成了《唐·乔万尼》(1787)、《魔笛》(1791)和《安魂曲》等不朽杰作。1791年，莫扎特在创作《安魂曲》期间病倒，12月5日在维也纳逝世，年仅35岁。关于他的死因有多种猜测，包括中毒、风湿热和肾脏疾病等。莫扎特的早逝使世界失去了一位音乐天才，但他留下的600多部作品对古典音乐产生了深远影响，至今仍被广泛演奏和研究。
points.descriptionEn: In 1787, Mozart was appointed as chamber composer to the Emperor, providing some financial security. This period marked the peak of his creativity, during which he completed immortal masterpieces including 'Don Giovanni' (1787), 'The Magic Flute' (1791), and the 'Requiem.' In 1791, while composing the 'Requiem,' Mozart fell ill and died in Vienna on December 5 at the age of 35. The cause of his death remains debated, with theories including poisoning, rheumatic fever, and kidney disease. Mozart's early death deprived the world of a musical genius, but his more than 600 works have had a profound influence on classical music, still widely performed and studied today.

supporter.zh: 莫扎特被尊为音乐史上最伟大的天才之一，他的作品完美融合了优雅、情感与技巧。支持者认为莫扎特的音乐超越了时代限制，展现了人类情感的深度和广度。他的歌剧改革了传统形式，交响曲和协奏曲达到了前所未有的高度，室内乐作品则展现了细腻的情感表达。莫扎特的音乐遗产不仅在于其技术上的完美，更在于其作品中蕴含的人文主义精神和永恒的美学价值，至今仍影响着世界各地的音乐家和听众。
supporter.en: Mozart is revered as one of the greatest geniuses in music history. His works perfectly blend elegance, emotion, and technical mastery. Supporters believe Mozart's music transcends temporal limitations, demonstrating the depth and breadth of human emotion. His operas reformed traditional forms, his symphonies and concertos reached unprecedented heights, and his chamber works showcased delicate emotional expression. Mozart's legacy lies not only in his technical perfection but in the humanistic spirit and eternal aesthetic values embedded in his compositions, continuing to influence musicians and audiences worldwide.

critic.zh: 批评者指出莫扎特的生活放纵且缺乏自律，财务管理不善导致他经常陷入经济困境。一些评论家认为他的某些作品过于华丽而缺乏深度，尤其是晚期作品中的某些段落被认为过于琐碎。此外，莫扎特对贵族阶层的依赖和迎合也被视为一种妥协，削弱了他作为艺术家的独立性。他的早逝部分归因于不健康的生活方式和过度工作，这些批评提醒我们天才也有其局限性和缺陷。
critic.en: Critics point out that Mozart lived a dissolute life with poor self-discipline and poor financial management, often leading to economic difficulties. Some commentators argue that certain works are overly ornate without sufficient depth, with some passages in his later works considered trivial. Additionally, Mozart's dependence on and accommodation of the aristocracy is seen as a compromise that weakened his independence as an artist. His early death was partly attributed to unhealthy lifestyle habits and overwork, reminding us that even geniuses have limitations and flaws.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，莫扎特被定义为古典音乐黄金时代的代表人物，他的名字已成为天才的代名词。历史学者将他置于启蒙运动和古典主义美学的背景下，分析其作品如何反映了当时的社会变革和思想潮流。流行文化中，莫扎特的形象被不断重塑，从电影《莫扎特传》中的浪漫化描绘到各种音乐节的致敬演出，他的音乐已成为西方文化的重要组成部分。莫扎特的生平和作品不仅代表了18世纪欧洲音乐的巅峰，也成为了人类创造力和艺术成就的永恒象征。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Mozart is defined as a representative figure of the golden age of classical music, his name becoming synonymous with genius. Historians place him within the context of the Enlightenment and classical aesthetics, analyzing how his works reflected contemporary social changes and intellectual currents. In popular culture, Mozart's image has been constantly reinterpreted, from the romanticized portrayal in the film 'Amadeus' to tribute performances at various music festivals. His music has become an essential part of Western culture, representing not only the pinnacle of 18th-century European music but also an eternal symbol of human creativity and artistic achievement.

self.zh: 音乐是比所有智慧和哲学都更高的启示。谁能参透音乐的意义，谁就能超越一切世俗的理解。
self.en: Music is a higher revelation than all wisdom and philosophy. He who grasps music can transcend all understanding of the mundane.

others.zh: 莫扎特是音乐的神圣火焰，我们其他人不过是凡人。
others.en: Mozart is the divine flame of music; the rest of us are merely mortals.
